title: How Much Does A New Roof Cost In Pennsylvania?
author: Admin
excerpt: Having to repair your roof can pose a challenge, especially when you have to replace the entire structure. The whole process can turn into a big inconvenience, and if not properly done, you’ll end up paying more money than you initially thought you would. As problematic as it can be if the situation calls for…
html:
Having to repair your roof can pose a challenge, especially when you have to replace the entire structure. The whole process can turn into a big inconvenience, and if not properly done, you’ll end up paying more money than you initially thought you would. As problematic as it can be if the situation calls for it, it should be attended to as soon as possible.

Expert Guide to New Roof Cost Estimates

Homeowners will have the option to select different price points for their roof replacement project. Keep in mind, however, lower-cost roofs will actually cost more over time because of the shorter life spans and early development of leaks.

Average roof costs change from state to state across the US, the national average for a new roof is between $8,000 and $15,000. However, the roof replacement cost can vary heavily on many variables, including the size of your roof, materials, and labor cost.

The Average Cost Of A New Roof In Pennsylvania

Materials needed for your roofing project are the biggest factor in any quote. Here are some average material costs per square foot in Pennsylvania.

Materials Average Cost per 100 square foot:

  • Asphalt Shingles – around $220
  • Tile Roof – around $970
  • Wood Shake -around $605
  • Metal roof – around $860
  • Slate roof – around $1,260
  • Flat roof – around $380

How To Know When It’s Time For A Roof Replacement

Sometimes repairing an existing roof is all that’s needed; however, there comes a time when even the best roofing repairs simply won’t cut it. That’s typically the time when you should start considering a roof replacement.

The following factors will help you determine whether or not your home requires a roof replacement.

Water Leaks

One of the more telling signs that your roof requires replacement is when you can notice water damage. Brown stains on your ceiling are a signal that your roof isn’t carrying out its main purpose of protecting your home from the outside elements.

One small water leak can be fixed with a quick repair job, but if a roof is letting in water over several different areas, it’s crucial that you take care of it by having a full roof replacement.

Missing or Damaged Shingles

Missing shingles or damaged areas are other indications that you are in need of a roof replacement. And changing weather can gravely impact the state of your home’s roofing.

Not only can rainy weather damage the roof, but you can also end up missing parts of your roof. So if you notice missing or damaged shingles, it’s definitely time to call a roofing professional.

The roof is Aged

Different types of roofing have different lifespans. For instance, while asphalt shingle roofing only lasts around 20 years, tile roofing can last up to 50 years. Factor in a few damaging storms, and you may need a roof replacement even sooner.

When you’re aware that you have a rather old roof, it’s advised to start thinking about hiring a professional roofing contractor – In The Light Roofing.

Our service area covers

Allentown, Macungie, Bethlehem, Emmaus, Whitehall, Easton, Coplay, Schnecksville, Slatington, and Hellertown.

What Factors Impact The Average Cost Of A New Roof In Pennsylvania?

Here are some of the variables that influence the new roof cost in Pennsylvania:

  • Zip code – urban areas often cost more for contractors than rural locations.
  • Choice of roofing materials.
  • Whether this is a new roof or an overlay that avoids paying labor for tearing down and dump fees.
  • The state of the roof deck when it is revealed – do you need any remedial work or repairs?
  • Roof features – is the design of your roof complex or a simple ranch style?
  • Are you adding skylights or dormers? This means extra materials and extra labor.
  • How steep is the pitch? Steeper roof planes always take more work.

What Are Additional Costs For Roof Replacement?

Extra costs will include:

  • Tearing down and dump fees unless you are opting for a roof overlay.
  • Scaffolding hire.
  • New skylights and dormer windows if you are replacing old fittings or adding in new features because you are also converting the roof space.
  • Costs for an architect or surveyor if you need drawings and plans.
  • Building permits.
  • Building inspection fees.

What Other Factors Impact The Choice Of A New Roof?

Budget is definitely one of the main things to consider when picking roofing material. However, one factor to also take into consideration is the general appearance of your house, meaning you are going to pick a roofing material that will go in line with the style of your home.

Most people will first choose materials based on appearance followed by longevity as a new roof is a large outlay, and you certainly want it to last. Somewhere in the mix will be value for money and price, meaning the dream option might just come in over your budget.

What a roof looks like is important in maintaining the value and curb appeal of your home but whether it is weatherproof and watertight is even more important.

Frequently Asked Questions

How Do I Know If My Roof Needs Replacing?

If you are unsure of your roof’s state, then be sure to ask a roofer to inspect your roof for you. Try to find a reputable roofer who isn’t just going to try and sell you a new roof even if you don’t need one.

You can look at your roof from the street, but you won’t be able to see the deck’s condition beneath as the shingles will obscure the view.

Annual roof inspections can provide peace of mind and repair smaller damages that can be easily and affordably remedied, resulting in the prolonged life of the current roof.

What Is A Roof Square?

Roof squares are used by many roofers and roofing materials retailers. One roof square equals 100 square feet. To determine how many roof squares your roof has, you can measure your roof and divide that number by 100, giving you the total number of roof squares.

Roof squares are an easy and convenient way to compare the cost of different roofing materials.

What Is The Best Choice Of Roofing Material For The Climate In Pennsylvania?

The prevailing weather across Pennsylvania can be defined as humid continental. Therefore, picking a roofing material that’s appropriate for this type of weather is crucial.

Asphalt shingles are one of Pennsylvania’s most popular roof options since they have a long life if the roof is well maintained. They are very easy to fit and work well in the Pennsylvania climate. Additionally, there is a range of designs and pricing options.

Final Words

When it comes to roof replacement in Pennsylvania, you have many options when it comes to materials and aesthetics. You have options for metal, asphalt, wood composite, tile, rubber, and many options for colors and styles in those categories. When you are in a place where you need a roof replacement in Pennsylvania, In the Light Roofing Contracting will be able to work with you and find the best option for your home and your budget.

title: How Many Layers Of Roofing Are Allowed In PA?
author: Admin
excerpt: It’s never a good scene when asphalt shingles reach the end of their lifespan. Signs include constant leaks, shingle loss, and mold that may force a roof replacement. However, replacing an asphalt shingle roof without a good budget can be overwhelming. Layers of Roofing: Risks and Benefits You need to reap off the existing roof…
html:
It’s never a good scene when asphalt shingles reach the end of their lifespan. Signs include constant leaks, shingle loss, and mold that may force a roof replacement. However, replacing an asphalt shingle roof without a good budget can be overwhelming.

Layers of Roofing: Risks and Benefits

You need to reap off the existing roof to install a new one. If your roof sheathing cannot handle the new roof, you will need to replace everything.

However, sometimes you want to apply a new roof shingle over your first layer. This will be applicable if your sheathing and roof structure is still intact. You can see recommendations from reputable roofing contractors.

But the question is, how many layers of shingles are allowed in PA? We will be answering this question here.

How Far to Take Your Roof Overlay

A full roof replacement can be expensive. There are expenses for buying new shingles and disposing of the old roof. According to the local building codes, you can have up to two layers of shingles on your existing roofs. Some people may want three layers, but that may only get you in trouble.

A second layer may be added, to your existing roofs, unless:

  • You already have a double layer of shingles or two or more roof covering applications.
  • The roofs feature slate, clay, or asbestos
  • The current material is water-soaked, or the roof structure is not strong enough to hold the second layer of shingles.

The roofing industry in every region has clear guidelines on how to deal with such issues. For example, the roof deck must be properly inspected to determine whether it’s eligible to hold more roofing components.

Experts will need to also check the roof flashing, the old shingles, and other roofing components to ensure they are all in good order. Even if your existing layer is in great condition, and the roof is eligible for re-roofing, industry experts will tell you multiple layers is not a professional approach.

Are There Benefits to More Than One Layer of Shingles?

We still encourage a complete replacement, especially for architectural shingles, which are more vulnerable to weather extremes. Nevertheless, depending on your roof’s pitch, you can have new shingles installed to make a double layer. Very rare occasions allow for three layers due to the risks they pose.

With proper installation, you should have more layers on your roofing system without many issues. Here are some of the benefits you can get:

Cost saving

It takes a lot of money to tear off a roof. There are significant costs involved when stripping the old roof and installing a completely new layer.

Aside from replacement costs, there are also costs to dispose of the old shingles and other materials. You can save on all of these costs by simply adding another layer.

Saves time

There is actually a lot of time involved in the entire replacement process. From the time you start stripping off the old roof to the time a new layer is instilled, you could have done so many things. Hence, you can take less time.

Also, the underlying wood will be exposed for too long as you lay the new shingles. This can be a problem when there is rain, say in the afternoon. It will soak the wood.

Possibly reduce the likelihood of ice dams

A second layer creates something like an ice shield over the shingles. Sometimes this can be a real problem during winter, affecting the integrity of your roofing system.

Should You Have More Layers of Your Roof Then?

In summary, multiple layers of shingles can reduce the labor costs involved in replacing the whole roof. It also makes the work easier. Buy should you do it?

Experts do not recommend it. A single layer of new shingles improves your home’s curb appeal while saving you on future costs. Here are the reasons why a full replacement is better than multiple layers of shingles.

Roofs are more than just layers of the material

For many homeowners, roofs are systems and not simply layers of shingles. The roofing system protects the home interior from elements like high winds and rain and keeps the energy in. It’s a system of barriers featuring flashing and counter flashing, waterproofing, a wooden roof deck, shingles, and more.

Adding on a second layer blocks you from checking the other elements. It becomes hard to inspect the roofs. Insurance companies will pay for a complete tear-off of the roof.

Re-covering affects the warranty

Even if you follow all the building codes, adding shingles to the first layer makes warranties void. Both the first layer and the second one is affected. If a manufacturer offers a 35-year warranty, the new layer will not have a warranty, and neither will the old one.

This can cost you more in case the roof has a serious issue. All roof components cannot be installed without removing the old ones.

Issues with insurance companies

You can claim a homeowners insurance policy, and the issuer will cover a complete replacement. This is because an inspection is carried out to reveal any rotten, deteriorated, or delaminated sheathing to understand what must be done. Some companies will not pay the insurance.

The extra weight

Shingles don’t normally weigh much per square foot. However, that extra 2 to 3 pounds can add up weight quite fast. Besides, second-layer shingles are often designed to weigh more to disguise missing shingles of depressions. Additionally, the fasteners like nails or staples must be longer and heavier.

Your building may need more structural strength to handle such factors. Or the roof could already be weak and damaged. The weight will initiate movement and settling of the house, which causes cracks in the foundation.

Future costs

You may avoid the roof replacement costs now, but understand that you will be dealing with more material when you want to replace the roof in the future. You now have two roofs, which could make disposing of them more expensive. Also, this can prevent flashing open valleys, chimneys, and similar areas from effectively.

Are You a Good Candidate for Roof-Overlaying

Certain roofing situations may require a complete tear-off, where repairs are no longer applicable. Homeowners in PA can have up to two layers of singles. Here are some conditions that are right for re-covering:

  • The roof itself is not rotten or damaged. Your roofer may need to thoroughly inspect the roof before determining its eligibility for an overlay. You can have another layer if the roof is still in good condition.
  • The damaged shingles are only on one side. An overlay can be a good idea if these shingles are one section of the roof, but the rest is good.
  • The majority of the roof does not require shingle replacement. If more than ¾ of your roof is still in great condition, you can avoid the cost of roof replacement.
  • Your roof only has one layer. Unless your roof already has multiple layers, your contractor may recommend another layer.

We recommend that you replace the existing material. But if you choose to use an overlay, then you must consider several factors. These include the warranty terms, extra weight on the roof, future repairs/replacement, and insurance coverage. Also, if your current roof is severally damaged, a full replacement is your best option. Let In The Light Contracting help you get a high-quality roof.

title: How Long Do Shingle Roofs Last In Pennsylvania?
author: Admin
excerpt: A roof is a considerable investment and one of the most important parts of your home. That is why you want it to last as long as possible. Hiring professional roofing contractors ensures such a roof. They will pick the right material based on the local weather. How Long Do Shingle Roofs Last In Pennsylvania?…
html:
A roof is a considerable investment and one of the most important parts of your home. That is why you want it to last as long as possible. Hiring professional roofing contractors ensures such a roof. They will pick the right material based on the local weather.

How Long Do Shingle Roofs Last In Pennsylvania?

In PA, asphalt shingles are among the most popular roof choices. Seeing a metal roof might take a while, but asphalt shingle roofs will be everywhere.

In this guide, we will be handling one of the biggest concerns for homeowners – how long do shingles last?

Factors Affecting the Lifespan of a Roof

As a stated table, roofs can be expensive to install. The lowest shingles cost about $70 per square foot. Metal roofs cost even more. That is why you may want to get the most from the material.

Consider the following, and you can estimate the best time:

Roofing material quality

A high-quality asphalt shingle roof can last for more than 20 years. This depends on the quality of the roofing materials. Always get your materials from a reliable brand and supplier.

There are so many categories of asphalt shingles. So, before you ask how long a roof lasts, you need to consider that material’s standard. One of the best ways to tell a quality roofing material is by checking the price. Highest-end materials often cost more.

The weather conditions

Weather is the biggest threat to a roof’s longevity. Pennsylvania is one of the regions in the world that experiences unpredictable changes in the environment. It can get extremely hot during summer and freezing during winter.

Prepare for a roof replacement much sooner if you don’t have a high-quality material on your roof system. Did you know that strong winds can easily blow off an asphalt roof? This can be another reason you want a roof replacement.

The quality of the installation

Asphalt shingles are one of the most common roofing materials in the USA, which is why you will easily find unqualified installers. Many homeowners complain about their roofing systems becoming a problem too soon.

Well, asphalt shingles require extra care during installation, even though they are easier to install than other materials. Always find a reputable roofer if you are installing a new installation or want to replace your roof. A good job assures maximum life from the roof. And you won’t be spending a lot of money on repairs before the time comes for it.

How Long Do Shingle roofs Last in Pennsylvania?

As stated above, there are various types of single roofs. Here is a breakdown of how much life they promise.

Traditional asphalt shingle roofs

First on the list is asphalt shingles, which are the most popular material. You will see them on more than 80% of PA homes.

Apart from affordability, traditional asphalt roofs come with up to 25 years of warranty. Proper maintenance can have a roof last for close to 30 years. Generally, asphalt roofs last for 15 to 30 years.

So, don’t be surprised if you start seeing roof leaks after 15 years. Unfortunately, the roofs have such a short life expectancy.

Asphalt shingles are made with an asphalt coating covering fiberglass or organic materials like cellulose. The asphalt offers a durable protective layer against environmental elements. The heat from the sun can soften a new roof quite easily, but it also bonds the shingles over time to create a watertight seal.

Each shingle type comes with advantages and limitations. Fiberglass roof shingles last longer than organic ones because they are designed with improved materials. But you will need an experienced contractor to enjoy these features.

The biggest limitation of asphalt shingles is their vulnerability to mold and fungus in humid areas. Even though they are installed on sloped roofs, they still face a huge threat from moisture retention.

In summary, get ready to start dealing with missing shingles and other issues on your shingle roof after 15 years. With such a short roof life expectancy, it’s no wonder asphalt is the most affordable roofing material.

Architectural shingles

Architectural shingles come with similar features to standard asphalt shingles. However, they are three times thicker, forming a denser and more resilient roof. Since a roof’s lifespan determines its warranty, you can get more than 30 years for these shingles.

Installing an architectural roof may not be as expensive as a tile roof, but it’s still much higher than asphalt and various other roofing materials. But the good news is that you can expect them to last for 25 to 30 years without considering a roof replacement project.

The multiple laminated layers of these roofs enhance their durability. They mimic other, more expensive materials like wood, slate, and tiles. Also, you can re-shape your existing roof to resemble any other material you want. The material promises incredible versatility.

Apart from durability and affordability, one of the most significant advantages of architectural shingles is ease-of installation. Many people have applauded them for allowing easy work across the roofs, including flashing of the roof valleys and when one wants their existing roof replaced.

Wood shingles

Wood shingles are quite strong. Cedar is the most popular choice for this material as it can withstand high winds and other weather conditions. If you maintain them well, with proper annual upkeep, wood shingle roofs can last for 15 – 30 years before replacing your roof. A wood shingle roof lasts longer than traditional ones, which is why they are also a trendy option.

Note that over time wood shingle roofs weather into a soft silvery gray and may look a different style altogether. They are best suited for Tudor and cottage-style houses featuring steep slopes.

In terms of installation costs, get ready to spend about $250 to $600 per square foot. From there, you can only be sure of a long-lasting roof if adequately maintained and depending on the specific material.

One of the main advantages of wood shingles is their aesthetics. They can be designed to mimic wood shakes and any other type of roofing material to meet specific needs. However, since they are natural, it’s quite easy to get several breakages during installation.

Also, they are vulnerable to discoloration, just like wood shakes. The roofs turn from their fresh brown appearance to a silvery grey. Some people prefer the new color, while others will want the original look.

How Long Does a Roof Last? Increase the Lifespan

Here are a few things you can do to ensure your shingles last long:

Inspection

Buckling shingles are a common problem on many shingle roofs. Many homeowners have experienced them, and some end up panicking too much. But it’s a common occurrence.

Individual shingles can curl or buckle over time when exposed to sunlight. These are also known as curling shingles. You can notice this effect if the areas where parts of the shingle have lifted.

A regular inspection can help you identify such issues much earlier and handle them before they become bigger problems. Call qualified inspectors and roofers at In The Light Roofing Contracting to get the issue fixed.

Buy quality material

Always check the warranty to determine the possible quality and durability of the material. High-quality material will last the longest if well maintained.

Maintenance

Clean your shingles regularly, replace missing shingles, and do other maintenance tasks on your roof. Asphalt shingles tend to last a bit longer when handled properly. Try wintering to protect your roof from harsh conditions. You can be sure to have a long-lasting shingle roof. If you can’t do any of these things, hire a qualified roofer to help you.

Hire an experienced roofing contractor

There no better way to get more years from your shingle roofs than using a qualified installer. You need someone who knows how to handle shingles. They will install in way that ensures longevity. Whether it’s a new installation or finding roof replacing shingles, you can always count on such a service.

title: Can You Still Live In Your Home While It Is Being Reroofed?
author: Admin
excerpt: When the time comes to have your roof replaced, there are several concerns that arise. One of the main ones is whether you can stay in the house while the roofing contractor is working. Can You Still Live In Your Home While It Is Being Reroofed? The simplest answer is yes. Many roof replacements in Bethlehem,…
html:
When the time comes to have your roof replaced, there are several concerns that arise. One of the main ones is whether you can stay in the house while the roofing contractor is working.

Can You Still Live In Your Home While It Is Being Reroofed?

The simplest answer is yes. Many roof replacements in Bethlehem, PA, happen without forcing the homeowners out.

Great roofing contractors understand some of the challenges that come with owning a house. Raising kids, paying the mortgage, working on utilities, and many other expenses can be quite overwhelming. Hence, you want to save as much as possible on any home renovation project, and hence, moving to another place is not an option.

What to Expect During the Roof Replacement Process

Most roof replacement projects can be done easily without sending the homeowner out. However, there are several things to keep in mind:

There will be constant banging

You will have the roof replaced easily, but expect to deal with too much noise. During roof replacement, there will be a lot of hammering, moving materials, talking, footsteps, and all kinds of noise in your home.

And that is why many homeowners prefer to stay outside when the roof replacement begins. If you are not very comfortable staying close to noisy areas, this is not the ideal condition.

Luckily, there are a few things you can do to avoid the noise and allow the roof replacement project to continue smoothly. Here is what to do:

  • Consult your roofing expert to start with one side of the house. This leaves the other part free from any disturbance.
  • Use noise dampeners. Most homeowners will put on earplugs and similar materials to stay away from the noise. A good roofing company may also recommend other ways to avoid noise.
  • Move to the basement. Another great idea would be moving to the basement. It may still be noisy, but not as much as when you are directly under the roof.

So, be ready to deal with noisy scenarios while replacing the roof. If you have no problem with that, everything should be ok.

Falling debris

If you must stay home during roof repairs, prepare to deal with falling objects. This will happen a lot, especially when the old roof is too damaged and everything has to be replaced. The roofing job will involve a lot of parts, which may be dangerous.

So, apart from dealing with loud noises, this debris can give you a stressful time. It can turn into a nightmare scenario if you don’t plan it well from the beginning.

Luckily, the best roofing contractors will always find a way to keep your house safe. For instance, they will ensure the ceiling is properly installed and strong before starting the roofing project. This should make staying home much easier.

Aside from that, you can:

  • Move to safe spaces for a few days until the work is completed.
  • Ensure your indoor and outdoor furniture is properly covered during the reroofing project.
  • Stay outdoors during the day and move inside only when the day’s work is done.

Falling debris can cause serious damage and injuries. Ensure proper precaution is taken before work begins. Consider the additional rules, like staying off active paths and work areas until the work is completed.

Other members of your house

If you choose to stay home during a roof replacement project, think about other members of the family living under the same roof. This is a key takeaway when it comes to managing the project properly.

Where are the kids? How will the pets react to all the commotion and noise? What about other people in the home?

Some may find it hard to stay inside during the process. It could be a great idea to consult and let them know what will happen. Those who choose to stay home should be ready for the outcome.

Whatever you do, the safety of your house matters more than anything else. Here are some tips to help you stay safe:

  • Keep off the contractor’s path. Find a safe place for your children and pets, and ensure they don’t come near the work area.
  • Stay outside during the day. If you don’t have anywhere else to go, stay outside as much as possible.

html:
Even with the highest quality roofing materials, a roof replacement is necessary after some time. It reaches a place where it can no longer hold the pressure, especially with the harsh weather conditions of Bethlehem, PA.

One of the biggest questions we have come across concerns the best time to replace a roof. When should you call for roof replacements?

What Is The Best Time Of Year To Have Your Roof Replaced?

In our experience, fall is the best time to get a good job done on your house. Even though most roofing contractors will be busy during this time, it should be a perfect atmosphere, especially if you book early enough.

There is no problem if your roofing contractor can work any time of the year though. It all comes down to getting the best roof over your home and your urgency.

We have highlighted the advantages and limitations of roof replacement during different seasons below:

Spring Roof Replacement

Early spring is a popular season to replace your roof for a few reasons. First, it comes right after the cold winter temperatures.

As the harsh weather conditions fade, more enjoyable conditions set in, encouraging many homeowners to start thinking about home improvement projects. Roof replacements are the perfect solution when roof leaks, drafts, cave-ins, or constant repairs may be too much to handle.

You need a good time to take care of those missing shingles. The spring weather is not as cold as winter, hot as summer, or busy as fall, making it the best time of the year to replace the roof. The cooler temperatures make the replacement process easy and efficient.

However, planning can be difficult, considering the unpredictability of the weather. Serious roof damage can happen when the rains or high heat during some part of the day interrupt the process. This can lead to details.

And that is why we recommend working with experienced roofers. They will come prepared for the conditions and find the best way to accommodate them.

Summer Roof Replacement

Summer is one of the busiest times for most roof installers. Early summer, especially, provides the best conditions for replacing asphalt shingles. The roofing materials harden better and faster since there are not much rain and the days are longer.

Call your roofing company in late spring and early summer. The rains have stopped, the extreme heat is still far, and the humidity is mild in the air. It’s an excellent time to replace your roof.

However, this is the most difficult time to schedule a re-roofing project. Many roofing companies will be working on completing their projects, prices will go up, and time slots will be too few. Many homeowners plan to avoid extreme temperatures in the summer heat.

Since it’s the busiest season, your project may be pushed too far into the extreme heat. Roof installations become too challenging as the sun produces more heat, which can melt the materials. It will be hard to get good roof work when the material gets constantly affected.

Call our roofers early enough to schedule your next roofing project during the mild weather conditions in early summer. We will ensure your roof is fixed before the higher temperatures hit, making it more durable.

Fall Roof Replacement

Late summer and early fall are other popular times when many roofing companies will be glad to work on your house. The summer season is ending, offering a great combination of cooler and consistent weather conditions.

An experienced roofing contractor will advise you to get a new roof now in preparation for the cold, snow, ice, and sleet. The comfortable temperatures offer the best roof replacement options, as the clear weather allows roofers to work with various materials.

Generally, the temperature is between 45F and 85F, with fewer rain threats, making it ideal for a new roof installation.

However, scheduling your roof installment project can be a bit challenging. Many people will be looking for the service, which can push your appointment into the blistering cold temperatures of late fall and early winter.

If you wish to replace your roof during fall, plan. Call your roofing consultant at least two months early or as soon as you notice a leaking roof.

Winter Roof Replacement

The extreme cold temperatures make winter a slow season. Hence, some people think replacing a roof is not a good time. However, it could be the best time for the job.

The harsh winter season creates more roofing contractors’ availability, ensuring your project is completed on time. However, be ready to reschedule when the weather conditions are too extreme.

Some contractors can still install a roof, especially when the weather cooperates. The problem comes when the temperature drops below 40F.

Since singles need thermal sealing to set, colder temperatures can delay the process. Ice accumulation can also make it even harder to work on the roof, damaging roofing materials.

Don’t wait for good weather to call for emergency repairs. It’s possible to work on some parts, like fixing leaking roof shingles. You can also replace the entire roof, especially if the roofer understands the conditions and what they are doing.

Call Us Now for your Next Roofing Project

A reliable roofer guarantees top-notch work, no matter the conditions. And that is what we promise.

Get in touch with our team at “In The Light Roofing” by calling (484) 232-1770 and get a free estimate or schedule your next home improvement project.
